articles.title: Sunday in Japan: A Ugandan asylum seeker turns to filmmaking
articles.summary: Facing deportation from Japan, a Ugandan filmmaker makes a samurai film inspired by his own life.
articles.body:
For more than 15 years, Sunday, a Ugandan asylum seeker, has lived in limbo in Japan. Once detained at the Shinagawa immigration centre, he must now regularly report to the authorities and rely on charity to help feed his children.

Changes to Japan’s immigration laws mean he could face deportation. Refusing to be reduced to a statistic, Sunday throws himself into an unlikely project: a samurai film inspired by Yasuke, remembered as Japan’s first Black samurai. For Sunday, filmmaking becomes an act of survival, dignity and hope.

Sunday in Japan is a documentary film by Antonio Rui Ribeiro, Leo Nelki and Golriz Kolahi.

articles.title: Guaíba e Jacuí sobem: Porto Alegre e Eldorado têm alagamentos | G1
articles.standfirst: Água invadiu ruas e pátios na Região Metropolitana nesta quinta-feira (1º). Capital tem obras de proteção no Gasômetro e alerta vigente para o bairro Arquipélago.
articles.summary: Nível do Guaíba e do Rio Jacuí sobe e provoca inundações em Porto Alegre e Eldorado do Sul, levando à instalação de comportas e alertas de risco.
articles.body:
A elevação dos níveis do Rio Jacuí e do Lago Guaíba já provoca alagamentos em Eldorado do Sul e na região das ilhas de Porto Alegre nesta quinta-feira (1º). Ainda que a chuva tenha dado trégua, a subida acontece após a elevação de rios ao Norte do estado.

Ao meio-dia, o nível do rio Jacuí, em Eldorado do Sul, chegou a 3m52cm, superando a cota de inundação, que é de 3m10cm. Equipes da Defesa Civil retiraram moradores de áreas de risco.

Na capital gaúcha, a água já atinge ruas da Ilha da Pintada . A Defesa Civil estadual emitiu um alerta vermelho indicando risco muito alto de inundação do Guaíba nas Ilhas , válido até as 11h10 de sexta-feira (2). Já o alerta da Defesa Civil Municipal para o bairro Arquipélago e áreas ribeirinhas das regiões Sul e Extremo Sul vigora até as 12h de domingo (4).

As equipes municipais realizam rondas para monitorar os impactos. A orientação dos órgãos de segurança é para que a população evite áreas inundáveis e consulte os planos de contingência. Em caso de emergência, abrigos da prefeitura podem entrar em operação.

Como medida de prevenção no Centro Histórico, a prefeitura de Porto Alegre iniciou a instalação de comportas de proteção contra cheias no prédio da Usina do Gasômetro.

Ao todo, 46 estruturas metálicas herméticas ficam instaladas no primeiro andar do edifício nos próximos 60 dias, para impedir que a água entre pelas portas e janelas. A obra tem investimento de R$ 690 mil e é executada pela Secretaria Municipal de Obras e Infraestrutura (Smoi). O projeto também incluiu a concretagem da câmara de resfriamento que ligava o prédio ao Guaíba.

"A Usina do Gasômetro é um patrimônio de Porto Alegre que está prestes a reabrir para visitação do público, mas uma estrutura histórica também nos impõe o desafio de construir uma proteção que preserve as características originais", afirmou o prefeito Sebastião Melo.

articles.title: Irmão desabafa após jovem morrer de câncer aos 23 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Camile Vitória Araújo de Souza, de 23 anos, lutava contra a leucemia linfoide aguda (LLA-B). Missa de sétimo dia será realizada nesta quinta-feira (1º).
articles.summary: Camile Vitória Araújo de Souza, de 23 anos, lutava contra a leucemia linfoide aguda (LLA-B).
articles.body:
O irmão da jovem Camile Vitória Araújo de Souza, de 23 anos, que morreu durante o tratamento contra a leucemia linfoide aguda (LLA-B) , fez um desabafo nas redes sociais. Zé André, conhecido por compor músicas de sucesso no sertanejo, escreveu que a irmã estará sempre viva no coração e na memória da família.

"Eu não faço ideia de como vai ser a vida sem você daqui pra frente. Mas se ela foi tão boa enquanto você esteve aqui, mesmo nesse mundo cheio de maldade, dor e sofrimento, imagina como vai ser na glória de Deus, quando estivermos juntos novamente. Esse é o refrigério da minha alma", escreveu.

Camile morreu no dia 25 de setembro, quatro meses após receber o diagnóstico. Em seu perfil no Instagram, a jovem compartilhava conteúdos sobre as diferentes fases do tratamento , a recuperação e a fé.

A missa de sétimo dia em homenagem à Camile será realizada nesta quinta-feira (1º), às 19h30, na Paróquia Rosa Mística, em Goiânia .

Filha de radialista morre aos 23 anos com leucemia em Goiás — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram Camile Vitória

Filha do radialista Luciano Sassinhora, Camile descobriu a leucemia linfoide aguda em maio deste ano. Segundo ela, os primeiros sinais foram uma forte dor de garganta, seguida pelo surgimento de hematomas pelo corpo, principalmente entre os dedos, além de fraqueza intensa.

A jovem suspeitou de anemia, mas exames de sangue apontaram alterações. Na sequência, uma biópsia da medula óssea confirmou o diagnóstico.

Em junho, Camile compartilhou o momento em que realizou o primeiro corte no cabelo. Segundo a jovem, o momento teve um significado especial para ela.

“Foi um processo cheio de risadas, leveza e diversão. Nada tem sido mais forte do que a força que Deus tem me dado todos os dias, e minha família tem sido meu maior suporte nessa caminhada.”

articles.title: Estudante de Medicina morto em Taubaté é enterrado em Jacareí | G1
articles.standfirst: Bruno Hashimura San Juliano, de 23 anos, foi baleado durante uma discussão no trânsito na Avenida do Povo. Bombeiro acusado de fazer os disparos teve liberdade provisória concedida pela Justiça.
articles.summary: O estudante de Medicina Bruno Hashimura, morto em briga de trânsito em Taubaté, foi enterrado em Jacareí sob pedidos de justiça após a soltura do bombeiro acusado.
articles.body:
Bruno Hashimura San Juliano, de 23 anos, foi enterrado na tarde desta quinta-feira (1º), no Memorial do Vale, no Jardim Califórnia, em Jacareí . O enterro começou por volta das 14h30 e durou cerca de uma hora.

O estudante de Medicina foi morto a tiros na manhã de quarta-feira (30), após uma discussão no trânsito na Avenida Professor Walter Thaumaturgo, conhecida como Avenida do Povo, em Taubaté .

Bruno era aluno do 4º semestre de Medicina da Universidade de Taubaté (Unitau). Ele foi baleado durante a discussão, chegou a correr após os disparos, mas não resistiu aos ferimentos.

Um vídeo obtido pela TV Vanguarda mostra o estudante correndo pela rua logo depois de ser baleado. Nas imagens, Bruno aparece colocando a mão no peito enquanto se afasta do local.

Segundo a polícia, foram disparados de quatro a cinco tiros. A perícia ainda deve apontar quantos disparos atingiram o estudante e esclarecer a dinâmica do crime. Um canivete foi apreendido dentro do carro de Bruno.

Estudante de medicina foi enterrado em Taubaté nesta quinta-feira. — Foto: Foto 1: Reprodução/Unama Santarém. Foto 2: Bruna Capasciutti

Testemunha e defesa apresentam versões diferentes

A defesa do bombeiro e uma testemunha ouvida pela polícia apresentam versões diferentes sobre o que aconteceu antes dos disparos.

Segundo a testemunha, Marcos desceu do carro e começou a gritar com Bruno. Depois, teria dado três cotoveladas no vidro do veículo até quebrá-lo. Na sequência, efetuou os disparos.

Ainda de acordo com o relato, Bruno permaneceu dentro do carro, com os vidros fechados, sem discutir ou fazer qualquer movimento para fora do veículo.

Bombeiro é levado em viatura após prisão em flagrante em Taubaté. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Vanguarda

Já a defesa afirma que o bombeiro havia tido um primeiro contato com Bruno ainda no túnel de entrada de Taubaté. Segundo o advogado Claudio Rodrigues, o estudante teria xingado e ameaçado a esposa do militar com um objeto que parecia ser uma arma.

Os dois teriam se encontrado novamente pouco depois, na região da Avenida do Povo, quando os carros pararam em um semáforo.

A defesa afirma que Marcos desceu do veículo, identificando-se como policial e pediu que Bruno saísse do carro. Segundo o advogado, quando o bombeiro se aproximou, o vidro do veículo estourou e o estudante voltou a fazer ameaças. Foi nesse momento, segundo a defesa, que o militar efetuou os disparos.

A polícia apreendeu um canivete no carro de Bruno. Nenhuma arma de fogo foi encontrada com o estudante.

Bruno foi descrito por colegas como uma pessoa alegre, otimista e bem-humorada. Amigos disseram que ele costumava alegrar os dias de quem estava ao redor.

"Era uma pessoa incrível, era uma pessoa extremamente alegre, nunca havia visto uma pessoa tão otimista quanto ele. Ele trazia sempre um bom humor para a gente, alegrava nossos dias. Algo completamente sem sentido (o assassinato). E agora a gente quer justiça por tudo isso", disse um colega.

Após a morte do estudante, a Unitau suspendeu as aulas do curso de Medicina na quarta-feira (30) e nesta quinta-feira (1º). A universidade também disponibilizou acolhimento e atendimento psicológico para alunos e professores.

Bruno Hashimura San Juliano — Foto: Reprodução

Bruno foi baleado durante uma discussão de trânsito na Avenida do Povo, em Taubaté. Ele foi socorrido pelo Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) e levado ao Hospital Regional, mas não resistiu.

Marcos Paulo Fujarra de Oliveira foi preso em flagrante e, neste momento, responde por homicídio doloso. A classificação do crime pode mudar durante o andamento da investigação.

A Justiça concedeu liberdade provisória ao bombeiro durante audiência de custódia nesta quinta-feira (1º).

articles.title: Drama aéreo vira munição eleitoral na disputa acirrada em Israel | G1
articles.standfirst: Aliados de Netanyahu associam tentativa de copiloto de derrubar avião a alerta de atentado anunciado na véspera pelo premiê; oposição acusa governo de explorar politicamente a segurança do país.
articles.summary: Aliados de Netanyahu associam tentativa de copiloto de derrubar avião a alerta de atentado anunciado na véspera pelo premiê; oposição acusa governo de explorar caso politicamente.
articles.body:
O alívio pela catástrofe aérea evitada por heroicos passageiros no trajeto entre Dubai e Tel Aviv deu rapidamente lugar à briga política em Israel , na tensa campanha que o país enfrenta para as eleições do próximo dia 27.

Aliados do premiê Benjamin Netanyahu correram para associar o incidente a um atentado jihadista , o que confirmaria o alerta que ele fizera, na véspera, sobre o plano de um ataque de inimigos antes do pleito.

O atual líder da oposição, Yair Lapid, desmereceu a advertência que ouvira na noite anterior do primeiro-ministro e contestou sua ligação com a tentativa frustrada do copiloto da Flydubai de derrubar o voo.

“Nada que sequer se assemelhasse remotamente ao incidente com o avião desta manhã foi mencionado na reunião de segurança com o primeiro-ministro ontem à noite. Toda essa narrativa que os porta-vozes estão propagando agora só comprova o que já estava claro ontem: que, mais uma vez, estão tentando fazer política barata às custas da segurança de Israel. Um bando irresponsável”, afirmou Lapid.

Premiê mais longevo do país, Netanyahu se encontra em dificuldades para formar um futuro governo, segundo as pesquisas de opinião , assim como seu principal oponente, Gadi Eisenkot, ex-chefe do Estado-Maior das Forças de Defesa de Israel: ambos os blocos ainda não teriam maioria para assegurar o mínimo de 61 cadeiras no Parlamento.

Netanyahu com Yaniv Hayun, passageiro da flyDubai que ajudou a subjugar copiloto que tentou derrubar avião — Foto: GPO via REUTERS

Pressionado por denúncias de que foi avisado com antecedência sobre o massacre de 7 de outubro de 2023 ao país e nada fez, o premiê está em situação mais complicada, desgastado aos olhos da opinião pública pela forma como lidou com as ameaças que culminaram no maior atentado em solo israelense.

Desta vez, ainda que o premiê não tivesse agido diretamente para conter o incidente, os israelenses saíram vitoriosos, e ele soube tirar proveito político da situação, capitalizando a euforia do país, ao lado dos sobreviventes.

Na véspera, o primeiro-ministro exibia, da base da Força Aérea, um ar soturno para advertir, sem dar detalhes, que recebera indícios de um ataque antes das eleições.

“Não se metam conosco — nem agora, nem nunca. Nosso longo braço os alcançará em qualquer lugar e a qualquer momento”, avisou.

Em vídeo, Netanyahu alerta para possibilidade de ataque antes da eleição em Israel — Foto: Jna Editor/JNA via ZUMA Press Wire/Reuters

Os candidatos opositores exigiram explicações sobre as ameaças relatadas por ele, e coube ao atual líder da oposição reunir-se com o premiê. Lapid diz ter saído do encontro sem se convencer de que havia uma ameaça concreta ao país.

"Não há motivo para causar pânico na população. Ameaças à segurança devem ser tratadas com profissionalismo e responsabilidade. A segurança de Israel e as bases das Forças de Defesa de Israel não são cenários para vídeos eleitorais”, afirmou.

O drama aéreo, um dia após o alerta de Netanyahu, pode ter sido uma coincidência, mas deflagrou um debate político acirrado. Seus opositores não demoraram a associá-lo ao 7 de Outubro, como fez duramente o ex-primeiro-ministro Naftali Bennett, que integra, com Lapid, a coligação Juntos.

“Eu não preciso que o governo me avise, preciso que ele me proteja.Você não é um aplicativo de alertas, você é o primeiro-ministro de Israel. Se você suspeitasse de que havia perigo de um avião explodir, o que você faria a respeito? Começaria a assumir a responsabilidade pela segurança. É exatamente como em 7 de Outubro”, resumiu.

articles.title: Sociedades médicas pedem à Anvisa proibição total de implantes hormonais manipulados no Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Carta divulgada durante congresso internacional de menopausa alerta para riscos dos chamados 'chips da beleza' e pede o fim da produção, comercialização e uso dos produtos. Em maio, investigação do g1 revelou como médicos e farmácias exploram brechas regulatórias para manter esse mercado.
articles.summary: Carta divulgada durante congresso internacional de menopausa alerta para riscos dos chamados 'chips da beleza' e pede o fim da produção, comercialização e uso dos produtos. Em maio, investigação do g1 revelou como médicos e farmácias exploram brechas regulatórias para manter esse mercado.
articles.body:
Doze entidades médicas e científicas nacionais e internacionais pedem à Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa) a proibição total dos implantes hormonais manipulados no Brasil, conhecidos popularmente como "chips da beleza".

O pedido está na Carta do Rio de Janeiro, divulgada nesta quinta-feira (1º), durante o 20º Congresso Mundial de Menopausa, realizado na capital fluminense.

Entre as entidades que assinam o documento estão a Sociedade Brasileira de Endocrinologia e Metabologia (SBEM), a Federação Brasileira das Associações de Ginecologia e Obstetrícia (Febrasgo) e a Sociedade Internacional da Menopausa (IMS).

Também assinam a carta a Sociedade Brasileira de Diabetes (SBD), a Associação Brasileira de Estudos em Medicina e Saúde Sexual (ABEMSS), a Associação Brasileira para o Estudo da Obesidade e da Síndrome Metabólica (Abeso), a Sociedade Brasileira de Urologia (SBU), a Associação Brasileira de Climatério (Sobrac) e as sociedades brasileiras de Mastologia (SBM), Reprodução Humana (SBRH), Cardiologia (SBC) e Hepatologia (SBH).

As entidades alertam que os implantes, frequentemente vendidos como solução para sintomas da menopausa, alterações na libido, emagrecimento e ganho muscular, não passaram por estudos clínicos de qualidade que comprovem os benefícios anunciados ou garantam a segurança de seu uso.

A carta também denuncia a expansão de um modelo comercial que envolve produção em escala, formação de estoques, treinamento de médicos para prescrever os produtos e divulgação nas redes sociais.

Em maio, uma investigação do g1 revelou como esse mercado continua funcionando apesar das restrições sanitárias. A reportagem identificou médicos que prescrevem os implantes, oferecem cursos sobre sua utilização e mantêm vínculos comerciais com farmácias de manipulação.

Documentos obtidos pela reportagem mostraram que implantes comprados por cerca de R$ 200 chegam a ser revendidos às pacientes por valores entre R$ 4 mil e R$ 12 mil.

Agora, as entidades querem que a proibição seja acompanhada de fiscalização mais rigorosa, fortalecimento da notificação de efeitos adversos e responsabilização dos envolvidos na cadeia comercial.

A discussão se arrasta desde outubro de 2024, quando a Anvisa determinou a suspensão da manipulação, comercialização, propaganda e uso de todos os implantes hormonais manipulados.

Após uma série de recursos administrativos apresentados por médicos, clínicas e farmácias, a agência voltou atrás no mês seguinte e substituiu a proibição total por regras mais restritivas.

Desde então, permanece proibida a comercialização e o uso de implantes hormonais manipulados à base de esteroides anabolizantes ou hormônios androgênicos para fins estéticos, ganho de massa muscular e melhora do desempenho esportivo.

A manipulação, entretanto, continua permitida em condições específicas para outras finalidades terapêuticas.

Na investigação publicada em maio, o g1 revelou como essa possibilidade abriu espaço para que implantes com ação anabolizante continuassem sendo oferecidos como tratamento para menopausa, endometriose e síndrome dos ovários policísticos, apesar da falta de evidências robustas para essas indicações nessa forma de uso.

As sociedades médicas defendem que a autorização excepcional para a manipulação individualizada não pode servir para manter um mercado de produtos sem os estudos exigidos dos medicamentos registrados.

"Prescrição individualizada não significa experimentação sem evidência e segurança", afirmam.

A nova carta solicita que a Anvisa proíba a manipulação, a formação de estoques, a comercialização, a distribuição, a publicidade e o uso dos implantes hormonais manipulados, independentemente da finalidade.

Um dos principais problemas está na própria forma de administração. Inseridos sob a pele, os implantes podem continuar liberando hormônios durante meses.

Diferentemente de tratamentos em comprimidos ou géis, que permitem ajustes na dose ou interrupção do uso, os implantes nem sempre podem ser retirados completamente.

Caso a paciente apresente uma reação adversa ou seja exposta a concentrações hormonais excessivas, pode não ser possível interromper imediatamente o tratamento.

As entidades também alertam para a ausência de estudos que comprovem a qualidade farmacêutica, a estabilidade, a esterilidade e a velocidade de liberação hormonal desses produtos.

Além disso, permanecem sem respostas questões sobre a segurança a longo prazo, incluindo riscos cardiovasculares, hepáticos, trombose, AVC e possíveis consequências para as mamas e o endométrio.

A gestrinona, um esteroide sintético presente em alguns implantes, também pode provocar acne, crescimento excessivo de pelos, queda de cabelo, alterações da voz e aumento do clitóris. Algumas dessas alterações podem persistir mesmo após a interrupção do tratamento.

Os riscos já aparecem nos consultórios. Em entrevista ao g1, o endocrinologista Clayton Macedo, doutor pela Universidade Federal de São Paulo (Unifesp), relatou que atende pacientes com complicações graves após o uso desses produtos.

"Muitas dessas pacientes chegam internadas e não sabem exatamente o que foi implantado. E, diferentemente de outros tratamentos, não dá para simplesmente suspender — o hormônio continua sendo liberado no corpo. Em alguns casos, nem a retirada é possível", afirmou.

Proibição atingiria todos os tratamentos hormonais?

As sociedades médicas ressaltam que o pedido não representa uma oposição à terapia hormonal, que tem eficácia e segurança respaldadas por evidências científicas quando corretamente indicada e acompanhada.

Existem medicamentos registrados e estudados, disponíveis em apresentações como comprimidos, géis, adesivos e formulações vaginais, que permitem ajustar as doses e interromper o tratamento quando necessário.

No caso da testosterona, a única indicação para mulheres respaldada por consensos internacionais é o tratamento do transtorno do desejo sexual hipoativo na pós-menopausa, após avaliação clínica cuidadosa e com doses que mantenham os níveis hormonais dentro da faixa fisiológica feminina.

Não há evidências que justifiquem seu uso para emagrecimento, ganho muscular, aumento da energia ou longevidade.

O pedido das entidades também não abrange os implantes contraceptivos registrados na Anvisa, como o de etonogestrel, utilizado para prevenir a gravidez.

O objetivo é proibir especificamente as formulações hormonais manipuladas na forma de implantes que não passaram pela mesma avaliação de segurança e eficácia exigida dos medicamentos registrados.

articles.title: Câmara de Campo Grande define Mesa Diretora para o biênio 2027-2028 | G1
articles.standfirst: Composição foi aprovada por unanimidade; vereadores mantêm os mesmos nomes, mas haverá mudanças nas funções da Mesa.
articles.summary: Composição foi aprovada por unanimidade; vereadores mantêm os mesmos nomes, mas haverá mudanças nas funções da Mesa.
articles.body:
Mesa Diretora Câmara Municipal de Campo Grande — Foto: Divulgação/Câmara

A Câmara Municipal de Campo Grande definiu, nesta quinta-feira (1º), a Mesa Diretora que ficará à frente do Legislativo no biênio 2027-2028. A composição foi aprovada por unanimidade durante sessão extraordinária.

🔎 A Mesa Diretora é responsável pela condução dos trabalhos legislativos até o fim da atual Legislatura.

Apesar de mudanças nas funções, a Mesa Diretora será formada pelos mesmos nomes que integram a atual composição. Confira:

3º vice-presidente: Neto Santos (Republicanos)

3º secretário: Ronilço Guerreiro (Podemos)

O vereador Dr. Lívio, que atualmente ocupa a 2ª vice-presidência, passará a exercer a 1ª vice-presidência.

Já o vereador André Salineiro (PL), atual 1º vice-presidente, será substituído pela vereadora Ana Portela (PL), que assumirá a 2ª vice-presidência.

A eleição foi convocada em cumprimento ao artigo 17 do Regimento Interno da Câmara Municipal, que estabelece que a renovação da Mesa Diretora deve ocorrer entre outubro e dezembro do último ano do primeiro biênio do mandato.

A norma também determina que a posse dos eleitos ocorra no ano subsequente. As regras estão previstas na Resolução nº 1.440, de 2 de junho de 2026.

articles.title: Train speeded up past red signal before fatal Bedford rail crash
articles.summary: Investigators say the train accelerated after passing a red signal that was not normally active.
articles.body:
A train involved in a fatal crash had accelerated past a red signal that was rarely ever on, investigators have found.

Train driver Shaun Burton, 60, died and more than 160 people were injured when his London-bound service crashed into the back of another train on 19 June at Elstow, near Bedford.

The Rail Accident Investigation Branch (RAIB) has found the signal had not displayed a red light to any train before the crash during 2026.

The latest interim report said CCTV had shown the signal had displayed red correctly, and Burton had acknowledged it, but he had continued to accelerate and applied brakes only seconds before hitting the other train, which had earlier come to a stop.

The collision took place between two East Midlands Railway (EMR) services on Network Rail's Midland Main Line, about 2.5 miles (4km) south of Bedford station.

The driver of the first train, travelling from Nottingham to London, was learning how to operate a new type of train under the supervision of an instructor.

It stopped after receiving an Automatic Warning System (AWS) alert, despite the signal ahead displaying green.

Neither the driver nor the instructor recognised the alarm as an AWS warning, and it was not acknowledged within the required window. This caused the train's emergency brakes to be applied automatically.

When Burton's train approached from Corby, the signal was displaying red, although he acknowledged its AWS warning, he continued to accelerate.

RAIB said no train had previously been recorded passing the signal while it was red since records began in 1985.

On 9 July, after the crash, another train approaching the same signal received an incorrect AWS warning despite it displaying green.

The AWS equipment was later found to be positioned 16mm below rail level, outside the permitted tolerance. Investigators are examining whether this contributed to the incorrect warnings.

However, investigators found no evidence that the signal itself was faulty when it was tested after the crash.

RAIB said it would continue to investigate why Burton's train had passed the red signal, as well as the signal's positioning, visibility and status.

articles.title: Dungannon: Two men jailed for raping woman in underground car park
articles.summary: The rape offence took place in September 2023 when both men were 17 and some of it was recorded on CCTV.
articles.body:
Two men have been jailed for raping a woman in an underground car park in County Tyrone.

Luis Dos Martins Mariano, 20, with an address of Sloan Street, and Alcino Soares, 21, with an address of Braeside, also in Dungannon, both previously pleaded guilty to rape.

Both men moved to Northern Ireland from East Timor when they were younger.

The rape took place on 10 September 2023 when both men were 17 and some of it was recorded on CCTV. The victim was 19 at the time.

At Downpatrick Crown Court on Thursday the judge sentenced both men to six years, three of those will be served in prison and three out on license.

Both men appeared in court via video link from Hydebank prison.

Judge Richard Greene said the CCTV footage of the incident "makes for disturbing viewing".

He also commended the "bravery" of the victim coming forward and said she was a "survivor".

He said her impact statement was both "eloquent and moving".

Judge Greene said the victim was subjected to a "prolonged and humiliating ordeal" with Soares and Mariano taking turns to rape her.

"It should have been obvious to both of them she was intoxicated and she was less able to recognise the danger she was in, she was not capable of resisting this cowardly attack on her and she was not able to call for help," he said.

Judge Greene said taking her to a car park at this late time showed a "significant degree of planning and foresight".

When sentencing the men Judge Greene said he took into account their young age at the time of offending, their learning difficulties, the fact they had both entered guilty pleas, delays to the case and time they had already spent in prison.

Warning: This article contains details readers may find upsetting

During an earlier sentencing hearing last month, the court heard details of the rape.

During the hearing in Dungannon Crown Court on 3 September, the prosecution outlined the victim's account.

A Tetum interpreter was present in court and stood beside Soares and Mariano translating the prosecution's account.

The court heard that the victim had been on a night out in Dungannon on 9 September 2023.

She said she had been outside a fast food shop and was "quite drunk".

She said she was approached by two males who appeared to be East Timorese.

Her next memory is then of both men walking either side of her down an alleyway which led into a car park.

The victim recalled she had difficulty standing and could not talk properly.

The prosecution outlined that the victim said one of the males "started to rape" her while the other male kept watch and "stood laughing".

The prosecution said the victim also recalled being brought to the corner of the carpark were she was raped again.

She said the males eventually left her and she eventually got up and left the car park.

The prosecution also outlined CCTV in the car park recorded the events and that it was "consistent with the defendants pleas".

The prosecution said was it was clear the victim was "incapacitated and in a vulnerable state".

In March 2025, the pair appeared together at Dungannon Crown Court where Mariano admitted rape but Soares pleaded not guilty.

Numerous adjournments followed and just before Soares was due to stand trial, in October 2025 he pleaded guilty to rape.

At Dungannon Crown Court on 3 September 2026, a defence barrister for Mariano said he was "not disputing the harm caused by this case".

The barrister outlined how an expert report had found that Mariano had a "moderate learning disability".

The barrister said when it came to his client it was a question of "age, vulnerability and cognitive ability".

The defence barrister said there was no "challenge to the integrity and strength of the victim" and that she "clearly did not consent in this case".

Mariano's barrister outlined that his client had apologised and expressed his "shame and remorse" about what had happened.

Soares' defence barrister said his client was neither fluent in either Tetum or English.

The barrister said an expert report outlined that this "language deficit" had led to difficulties and impacted his "understanding of societal norms and morals".

The barrister said Soares apologised and had "accepted his wrongdoing and his remorse".

Both men were ordered to be on the sex offenders register for life.

They were also disqualified from working with children and young adults.

Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) Ch Insp Steph Finlay said the incident was an "appalling and deeply distressing attack on a young woman who should have been able to make her way home safely after meeting with friends".

"The actions of these two men were predatory, degrading and showed a complete disregard for their victim," the officer said.

I want to pay tribute to the tremendous courage she has shown throughout what has undoubtedly been an extremely difficult and traumatic process."

She said the sentences "hold both men accountable for their actions".

articles.title: Russian drone hits school in Ukraine’s Kyiv as Moscow presses air assault
articles.summary: Russian drone strikes hit a school in Kyiv and the main bridge, disrupting transport in the latest wave of attacks.
articles.body:
A Russian drone has struck a school in Kyiv, officials said, as the Ukrainian capital endured another day of bombardment.

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said children and staff were hiding in shelters when the drone hit and there were no immediate reports of casualties during the attack on Thursday.

Elsewhere, two Russian drones hit an important bridge connecting eastern and western Kyiv, forcing the suspension of metro services and ground public transport.

In a statement on Thursday, Ukraine’s nuclear safety watchdog said a Russian drone hit the grounds of a nuclear research facility in Kyiv on Wednesday, causing a fire but leaving the facility’s test reactor undamaged.

“The fire that resulted from the attack was quickly extinguished. There were no injuries,” the regulator said in a statement, adding that the reactor was not damaged and had been shut down since 2022.

Ukraine’s air force said the number of Russian drone strikes on the country increased in September, with 3,177 attacks up to September 29. In August, 2,850 attacks were recorded.

Meanwhile, local authorities in Russia’s Belgorod region said one man was killed when a drone exploded in the town of Graivoron on Thursday.

The attacks come as the United Kingdom announced a new package of 31 sanctions on Russia, aimed at stemming funding to the “Kremlin war chest, propagandists and torturers”.

In a statement, the UK’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office said the sanctions targeted “eight people involved in the arbitrary detention, torture and ill-treatment of Ukrainian civilians” and a further “seven individuals are being targeted for their role in the indoctrination and militarisation of Ukrainian children”.

It said it was not seeking confrontation with Russia but would support Ukraine until the end of the “barbaric” war.

articles.title: Attacker's early prison release left victim 'feeling like an afterthought'
articles.summary: Hannah Pritchett said she was not told for five months that her attacker had been freed from prison.
articles.body:
Hannah Pritchett was 18 when she was stabbed in the lower back and hip by her boss Luisa Santos.

She was about an hour into her waitressing shift in May 2022 at the Three Horseshoes pub in Princethorpe, Warwickshire, when the blade went in. It was a fish knife, and with its cuts came Santos's false accusation the teen had had an affair with her husband.

That October, Santos was jailed for 10 years after being convicted of attempted murder. She was released in January 2026 under the Early Removal Scheme, which allows foreign national inmates in England and Wales, under certain criteria, to exit prison before they would have previously been allowed for the purpose of deportation.

Pritchett did not know of her attacker's departure from prison until five months after the fact. Sharing with the BBC the scheme's effect on her, she said she had been made to feel like an "afterthought", which was "just appalling".

A Ministry of Justice (MOJ) spokesperson said: "This was an awful crime, and our thoughts remain with Hannah Pritchett. Keeping victims informed is a vital part of our work and we are committed to always improving our service."

When asked by the BBC what the timeline should be for victims being informed of an offender's release under the removal scheme, the MOJ said the intention was for all victims to be contacted as soon as possible once information was available.

In the case of Pritchett, who was informed by the Victims Liaison Unit in June, there was an administrative error, the MOJ said, adding the matter had been escalated to management in both that unit and the prison in question.

Santos was deported having served three years and eight months in prison. The BBC has also sought clarification on her native country.

"Foreign nationals deported under the Early Removal Scheme are banned from ever returning to the UK," the MOJ spokesperson said.

According to Pritchett, however, the situation had made her "see that victims aren't at the forefront of these decisions".

Now 23, she said she had expected Santos to remain in prison until 2032 and thought she would have that time in which to come to terms with what had happened.

"When you get told on a random Tuesday in June that your attacker is now out and [is not serving] their sentence any longer it makes you feel that everything you have fought for was for nothing," said Pritchett, who lives in Coventry.

"Receiving that news was incredibly difficult and left me feeling let down by the justice system."

"It was a reminder that although a sentence may come to an end, the impact on victims continues long after."

"I went through a very difficult time when I was told my attacker was released early, especially as I found out five months after – it made things so much worse," she said.

Pritchett underwent surgery in hospital following the attack and said she had been "incredibly lucky to survive".

Pritchett questioned whether hundreds of victims were going to be made aware that their attackers would be released.

"In my case an administrative error led me to find out five months after," she said.

"If someone's attacker is released in the UK, what happens if they go out one day and see them in the street without being made aware?"

She said victims should be "at the forefront" of decisions on early release.

"My case was horrendous and I wouldn't wish that on anyone."

As part of her recovery and healing, Pritchett now raises money for knife crime prevention charities.

She plans to walk the Great Glen Way in Scotland next year and is hoping to raise £5,000 and finish the challenge on the fifth anniversary of the attack.

"Five years ago, I was incredibly fortunate to survive - five years on, I'm choosing to keep moving forward," she said.

The MOJ said that offenders leaving prison from 1 October would be monitored under the "toughest supervision" with the "biggest ever expansion of electronic monitoring rolled out".

Offenders would be electronically tagged and monitored when they left prison and £700m was being invested in probation and community punishment, the MOJ added.

It said victims would be offered "better practical and emotional support" through a newly launched helpline operated by Victim Support.

articles.title: In 1997, this Odisha man left his job and built a seed bank that hands out traditional rice varieties to farmers; years later, Debal Deb's effort is rescuing India’s rice diversity
articles.summary: In 1997, ecologist and conservation scientist Debal Deb established Vrihi, a seed bank created to conserve traditional rice varieties and revive the older
articles.body: In 1997, ecologist and conservation scientist Debal Deb established Vrihi, a seed bank created to conserve traditional rice varieties and revive the older practice of exchanging seeds without treating them as a commercial product. Nearly three decades later, his collection has grown to 1,480 rice landraces collected from indigenous farmers in India and from farmers and conservationists in several other countries. At his 1.7-acre research farm in Rayagada district, Odisha, the varieties are grown every year so that their seeds can be regenerated and distributed. The Centre for Interdisciplinary Studies (CIS), which coordinates Vrihi, describes it as the first non-governmental rice seed bank for farmers. According to the official website of Vrihi, more than 8,000 indigenous farmers in 13 states had directly or indirectly received rice seeds from the seed bank as of June 2026. The seed bank is now located in Kerandiguda village in Bissamcuttack block of Rayagada district, Odisha.How Deb's seed bank beganThe search for disappearing traditional rice varieties began in 1995, according to the Vrihi website. Deb started looking in remote parts of western and northern West Bengal, where many tribal farmers were still growing locally adapted rice varieties. Vrihi was established in 1997 as part of the wider folk-crop conservation movement led by the Research Foundation for Science, Technology and Ecology. The name Vrihi comes from the Sanskrit word for rice. The project initially received support from the foundation until March 2000. Since then, according to CIS, Vrihi has operated through Deb's personal funding and donations from supporters.The rule: take a seed, give a seedVrihi's model is based on seed exchange rather than seed sales. According to its current seed-exchange protocol, any farmer can receive an indigenous rice variety free of cost from the seed bank. The farmer is expected to give around 1 kg of seed of at least one folk rice variety in exchange. That seed is then passed on to another farmer. If a farmer does not have a traditional variety to exchange, Vrihi allows the farmer to take a 1-kg packet after paying a security deposit. The deposit is refunded when the farmer returns 2 kg of that rice after harvest. The arrangement is intended to ensure that the seed is cultivated and multiplied rather than simply taken away and lost.Vrihi says traditional seeds were once treated as a community resource, exchanged among farmers, relatives and friends. The organisation argues that the spread of commercial seed systems and agricultural modernisation has contributed to the loss of many traditional crop varieties and local food cultures.1,480 varieties in the collectionThe scale of the collection is one of the most striking parts of Deb's work. As of April 2024, Vrihi listed 1,480 rice landraces in its seed stock. These were collected from indigenous farmers in India as well as from farmers and conservationists in countries including Bangladesh, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Korea, Italy and the Philippines. The collection contains rice varieties with unusual characteristics. One is Jugal, described by Vrihi as a double-grain rice variety. Another is Sateen, a triple-grain rice variety. Ramigali, from Chhattisgarh, has elongated sterile lemmas that resemble wings, while Kharah and Makhan have purple culms and leaves. Vrihi also lists Garib-sal, which it describes as the world's only landrace containing silver in its grains.The collection also includes varieties with different agricultural and nutritional characteristics. Vrihi says numerous landraces are rich in vitamin B complex, while around 30 contain two essential omega-3 fatty acids that it says are found only in mother's milk. The collection also includes varieties that can withstand drought, flooding or salinity, as well as varieties showing resistance to different pests and diseases.Every variety is grown, not simply storedThe work does not end with collecting seeds. Vrihi says all its rice varieties are cultivated at the Basudha research farm. Every year, samples of the varieties are taken from Vrihi and planted in small plots. Core sample panicles from each plot are then harvested and stored for the following season. Keeping hundreds of rice varieties close to one another creates the possibility of cross-pollination. To reduce that risk, the researchers use an approach based on asynchronous flowering, transplanting varieties with different flowering periods in neighbouring plots.More than 8,000 farmers in 13 statesThe organisation says its seed-exchange membership had grown from just 21 members in early 1998 to 1,680 by early 2015, covering eight Indian states. By April 2019, more than 7,600 farmers from 10 states had exchanged seeds of 910 rice varieties with Vrihi. As of June 2026, the Vrihi Seed Exchange Network had around 740 primary farmers who received seeds directly from the seed bank. Through these farmers and their subsequent exchanges, more than 8,000 indigenous farmers in 13 states had directly or indirectly received rice seeds from Vrihi. The farmers continue to grow and exchange the varieties among themselves.A national award and a long-term conservation effortVrihi received the National Plant Genome Saviour Award from the Plant Variety Protection and Farmers' Rights Authority, Government of India, in February 2009. Nearly three decades after Vrihi was established, Deb's system continues to work around the same basic principle: collect traditional seeds, grow them, document them and put them back into farmers' hands. The farmer can take the rice home, grow it and sell the harvest. The seed, however, is meant to keep moving from one farmer to another.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Blasts heard in Addis Ababa as Ethiopia conflict widens in the north
articles.summary: Thousands flee Mekelle amid advancing troops and disrupted services as tensions rise in Ethiopia’s northern territories.
articles.body:
Explosions have been heard in the Ethiopian capital as fighting between federal forces and a coalition of armed opposition groups widens in the country’s north.

The violence comes as Ethiopia said on Thursday that it will close its embassy in neighbouring Eritrea.

Three diplomatic sources told the Reuters news agency that blasts were heard overnight in Addis Ababa, hours after the government banned drone-flying over the capital city and surrounding areas. A source linked to Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival told the agency the rebel alliance had carried out several drone strikes in Addis Ababa, including some targeting the military’s headquarters.

The alliance unites seven armed groups, including the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) and groups from the Amhara, Afar, Somali and Benishangul-Gumuz regions, in an effort to remove Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government.

Alliance fighters have also clashed with government forces in the neighbouring Afar region , where the authorities have renewed accusations of an Eritrean incursion.

Ethiopia’s Foreign Ministry said in a statement that it will close its embassy in Eritrea’s capital, Asmara, after it ordered 10 Eritrean diplomats in Addis Ababa to leave the country within 48 hours.

The ministry accused Eritrea of “direct and indirect acts of hostility and belligerence against Ethiopia”. The Eritrean diplomats were expelled on Thursday over activities that pose “a direct threat to Ethiopia’s national security” in breach of the United Nations Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, the ministry said.

The ministry urged Eritrea to “cease all acts that are contrary to the principles governing relations between sovereign states”, saying it remains committed to “peaceful resolution of disputes” and regional integration in the Horn of Africa.

Eritrea has denied allegations that it is supporting the opposition alliance fighting Ethiopian government forces since last week.

Reporting from Afar on Wednesday, Al Jazeera’s Muhammed Taha Tawakel said fighting had moved from the Amhara region deep into Tigray as government forces advanced north, reaching within about 40km (25 miles) of Mekelle, its regional capital.

The TPLF, meanwhile, had pulled its fighters back to new positions, and some of its leaders had moved out of Mekelle, Tawakel said.

They were joined by thousands of civilians who fled the city fearing clashes, he said. Electricity and internet services in the region had been cut.

Last week, Tigrayan forces mounted a large offensive , which the TPLF calls a “defensive war” against federal drone and artillery strikes. Government troops and allied fighters have since launched a counteroffensive.

The federal government has accused neighbouring states of backing the coalition , which they deny.

In Afar, government forces told Reuters they have recaptured the towns of Erebti and Abaala near the border with Tigray. The claim remains unconfirmed.

On Wednesday, Al Jazeera’s Tawakel reported that the fight to control the towns was ongoing, and escalation in the northern region threatened to drag Ethiopia and Eritrea into a wider war.

He said mediation efforts by locals to persuade forces controlling Abala and Erebti to withdraw failed, and the situation of more than 80,000 Afar residents trapped in the area remains uncertain.

Tawakel said the fighting in Afar carries the risk of regional repercussions, potentially bringing Eritrea and Ethiopia into a wider war and poses a risk to food security if routes between Ethiopia and Djibouti are disrupted.

Fighting had also reached areas along Ethiopia’s borders with Eritrea and Sudan, he said, increasing the risk of regionalising the conflict.

Ahmed Hussein, Afar’s deputy governor, told Al Jazeera on Wednesday that Ethiopia had come under an unprecedented attack which he said sought to undermine the regional administration and install figures loyal to Eritrea.

He called on Asmara to withdraw from Afar territory and held it responsible for the safety of civilians in areas controlled by opposition groups.

articles.title: In the 1930s, Bob Anderson's grandfather bought a Montana ranch; nearly a century later, the family permanently protected all 884 acres from subdivision to keep it in agriculture
articles.summary: Some landscapes change almost imperceptibly. Fences are repaired, seasons come and go, generations take over, but the land itself remains much as it was.
articles.body: Some landscapes change almost imperceptibly. Fences are repaired, seasons come and go, generations take over, but the land itself remains much as it was. In Montana's Paradise Valley, one family has made sure that continuity will extend well into the future. Nearly a century after Bob Anderson's grandfather acquired a ranch southwest of Livingston, the Anderson family has placed all 884 acres under a permanent conservation easement, ensuring the property remains intact and available for agriculture, states a report by USDA's Natural Resources Conversation Service website.Located in the Trail Creek area, the historic ranch combines productive farmland, native rangeland and an important stretch of waterways. As per the USDA report, about 1.5 miles of Trail Creek runs through the property, attracting a diverse mix of wildlife, including elk, pronghorn, bears, sandhill cranes and numerous bird species. The ranch also borders protected private property and US Forest Service land, creating a larger landscape of connected habitat rather than an isolated parcel.Today the land is still a working agricultural property supporting grass hay and cattle production so its conservation is not simply about preserving scenery, it is about protecting farmland and rangeland from conversion to residential or other nonagricultural uses. As of the August 2025 report, the Anderson family have a multigenerational relationship with the property.Bob's ancestors, the Nesbits, arrived in Paradise Valley in the 1870s, following the Civil War. His grandfather purchased the ranch in the 1930s, and after his death in 1953, the property passed to Bob's mother. Bob eventually bought it from her in 1980 and has spent the past 45 years as its owner and operator.The decision to place the ranch under a conservation easement was driven by a desire to keep the property together and protect its agricultural future. Rather than allowing development pressure to gradually divide the land, the easement permanently restricts subdivision and ensures the ranch remains one contiguous agricultural property, explains the online report.The Andersons worked with Northern Yellowstone Open Lands, a regional initiative of Gallatin Valley Land Trust, with support from the US Department of Agriculture's Natural Resources Conservation Service through its Regional Conservation Partnership Program. The family donated a substantial portion of the property's value toward creating the easement, with the donation matched through private philanthropy secured by the land trust.The protection also has implications beyond the ranch boundaries. Keeping the property intact preserves open space, supports wildlife movement and helps safeguard water resources in the Upper Yellowstone River watershed.For a ranch that has remained remarkably consistent for generations, permanent protection offers a way to preserve not only land but a way of life. The fields will continue to produce hay, cattle will continue to graze, and Trail Creek will keep moving through the property.Images Courtesy: Wikipedia and USDAYou use AI every day. articles.title: Flydubai passenger describes hugging his children as plane nosedived during attack
articles.summary: Adam Polovincik tells the BBC he told his young children "everything is going to be all right" as flight plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m).
articles.body:
A man has described how he hugged and reassured his two young children as their plane suddenly descended after one pilot stabbed the other in an attempt to seize control of the flight.

A Flydubai plane plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m) in less than two minutes around two hours into its journey from Dubai to Tel Aviv on Wednesday, before passengers and crew overpowered him and retook control to land safely.

Adam Polovincik told BBC Newshour that he hugged his six-year-old son and three-year-old daughter "really hard" and tried to stay calm for them as the attack unfolded.

He praised the pilot who was stabbed and passengers who fought off and subdued the attacker, saying they were "true heroes".

The stabbed pilot is in a stable condition in hospital, while the alleged attacker has been arrested.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said it was too early to say whether Iran was involved in the attack , but that the alleged attacker had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination".

Polovincik, who was sitting in aisle 13, was flying home with his wife and children after an "amazing" holiday in Singapore and Thailand.

He said there had been a "huge degree of panic" on the plane as there was a "very, very, very sharp decrease in height".

What we know about stabbing on Flydubai flight to Israel

He thought at first that this was simply because of an air pocket, but "it took a lot of time, almost a minute".

Everyone who had not been seated fell to the floor, the 40-year-old said.

"After a couple of seconds, we started to hear screams. 'There is blood, there is stabbing, we need help'," Polovincik said.

"At the end of the day, you understand very, very quickly that literally there is nothing that you can do at this point in time," he said.

Polovincik, a performance marketing analyst, said he tried to "be cool" for his children.

"You just tell them, yeah, everything's going to be all right. It's just a malfunction in the aeroplane, there is a crew under control, the passengers are helping them, [you] hug them really hard and try to keep your face so it doesn't look very panicked, try to keep your tone of voice."

But he said there was naturally a "high degree of panic" on the flight.

There were lots of families with children on the plane because the flight took place towards the end of a Jewish holiday period.

After about 10 to 15 minutes, he said a passenger in the cockpit told them the incident was "under control" and other staff were flying the plane.

In a video released by Netanyahu's office, passenger Yaniv Hayun described putting the attacker in a chokehold and pulling him out of the cockpit before other passengers helped pin him down.

Two other pilots who were onboard the flight then took over the controls and safely landed the plane, which had been carrying more than 150 passengers.

Polovincik said: "After they told us that the situation is, again, 'under control', then it was a bit harder to tell the kids that it's malfunctioned because people start to walk around the aeroplane covered with blood."

Polovincik was praised Indian pilot, Capt Smit Machchhar, who fought off his attacker and opened the door to the cockpit, allowing passengers to step in.

"Without him opening the door, we're probably not speaking here right now," he said, adding that he "can't even start saying our gratitude for this human being".

Polovincik said that, although he was not religious, he could not escape "the feeling that it was the hand of God yesterday" that had put "the pieces on the board in the way that they did".

After the situation onboard was brought under control, the flight was diverted to Saudi Arabia, where Polovincik stressed the passengers, who were almost all Israeli, were treated well.

"They brought us water and food and coffee and even sweets for the kids - even though we don't have any diplomatic relationship between Israel and Saudi Arabia," he said.

The alleged attacker, who was arrested in Saudi Arabia, is expected to be transferred to the United Arab Emirates, from where the plane departed, Netanyahu told Fox News.

The passengers were taken to Tel Aviv on another flight later on Wednesday and were greeted at the airport by crowds of onlookers playing music, singing, dancing and waving Israeli flags.

Polovincik said it had been "such a terrible ending" to an amazing family trip and that it would take some time for his family to come to terms with what had occurred.

articles.title: What we know about the cockpit stabbing on Israel-bound flight
articles.summary: What we know about the potential midair disaster aboard the Flydubai flight when a pilot attacked his colleague causing the plane to plunge thousands of feet.
articles.body: Questions remain about how a pilot managed to sneak a weapon aboard a plane and stab his fellow pilot before it plunged thousands of feet in mere seconds. The attacker was thwarted, passengers said, and the plane made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. “We were so scared. We didn’t know what was going to happen,” Aviatar Alevi, a 17-year-old student, told NBC News on Wednesday after he and the rest of the passengers were flown to Tel Aviv. Here is what we know about the incident and how close it came to resulting in tragedy. What did passengers see? Alevi described a harrowing scene aboard the flight, with people “screaming, running, panicking, blood.” “At the start, I thought it was a plane malfunction, but then I started hearing screaming about the stabbings,” he said. “We didn’t know what was going to happen,” he said, adding that the possibility of death “was definitely an option.” Another passenger, Motti Cohen Or, 70, said that he heard a woman shouting that “someone is stabbing someone in the cockpit” before the aircraft dived “toward the ground.” Yaniv Hayun was pictured in a bloody T-shirt telling cameras he had been among those to enter the cockpit and subdue the attacking pilot. At Ben Gurion Airport, after the passengers had returned to Israel, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu thanked Hayun, whom he later identified as a plumber. Three others helped in the effort to save the plane and those aboard, Hayun told reporters. The group struggled to open the cockpit door. “I grabbed the attacker, and choked him, pulled him out first,” he said. “I started pulling the controls.” “Thank God, we pulled it off. We really put our heads together and worked as a team,” he said. “It was between fear and a sense of a do-or-die situation.” “We had to win. We had to pull through and come out on top,” he added. Who is the hero pilot? Hailed as a hero, Indian pilot Smit ​Machchhar was credited by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on X for saving “the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals.” Even though he was bleeding heavily, Machchhar managed to unlock the door to the cockpit, Netanyahu told Fox News, allowing crew members and passengers to subdue his colleague and regain control of the plane. The Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia said in a post on X that he was admitted to hospital in Tabuk, where the plane landed, and was “reported to be in stable condition.” According to his LinkedIn profile, Machchhar, who was also praised on social media by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, worked with India’s SpiceJet ‌airline for more than 11 years before joining Flydubai. He has logged more than 9,750 flying hours, the profile says. Machchhar trained as a pilot at Mainland Air in the New Zealand city of Dunedin for 18 months, beginning in 2008, the school’s CEO, Philip Kean, told the country’s 1News outlet. Machchhar “did very well” as a student and later returned to India where he worked as a recruiter for the school, Kean said. What about the alleged attacker? Few details have been released about the alleged attacker, including his name and his condition. Two senior U.S. law enforcement officials briefed on the incident told NBC News that investigators say the pilot who began stabbing the other pilot is from Oman. Omani authorities have not commented and the Omani Foreign Ministry and the embassy in Washington did not respond to requests for comment from NBC News. Netanyahu said the pilot was being investigated in Saudi Arabia, where he was detained after the flight landed. Netanyahu added that he believed he would eventually be taken to the United Arab Emirates. Was this an attack? Based on the early results of the investigation, it increasingly looks like this was an act of terrorism, a senior American official and a Saudi Arabian official briefed on the investigation told NBC News. However, the Saudi official cautioned that the investigation was still in its early stages. No official statements on its investigations have been released by the kingdom. The United Arab Emirates, which owns Flydubai, is also trying to determine “whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or ‌purpose, or involved prior planning or direction,” the country’s state news agency reported Thursday. Without providing any evidence, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said Wednesday ⁠that preliminary information indicated that the pilot whom he described as a terrorist aimed to crash the plane. Netanyahu described it as “a serious security incident.” Speaking in the Oval Office on Wednesday, President Donald Trump said he had spoken with Netanyahu “at length about this event.” “It seems as though the co-pilot was perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack job, and he stabbed the pilot,” he said. Was Iran involved? There are no indications that Iran directed or was involved in the attack, a senior U.S. official briefed on the Israeli investigation told NBC News. And there have been no official suggestions from Israel that the Islamic Republic was behind the attack. Two Israeli security officials told The Associated Press that Israel had not identified any Iranian involvement so far. Does this alter anything for American flights? There are “no credible threats” to U.S. airlines, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told a news conference Wednesday. But he said the U.S. took every incident like this very seriously “and we continue to look at the procedures that we have in place, and continue to make sure the American people are safe.” What questions remain? Aside from his nationality, little is known about the pilot who carried out the attack or his motives for doing so. Pilots undergo rigorous screening and it is standard for airlines to vet their backgrounds and check their criminal and employment history. They also pass through metal detectors and checkpoints at airports, so it is unclear how he snuck a weapon aboard the plane. Netanyahu said in his interview with Fox News that Machchhar had apparently been stabbed or hit with ⁠an axe. It also remains unclear whether air marshals were on board the flight at the time of the incident. Saudi Arabia has warned that it is too early to draw definitive conclusions about who was responsible for the incident, and Israel and the UAE have announced investigations into what exactly happened on Flydubai Flight 1073.

articles.title: What we know about the pilot hailed as a hero for averting crash of Israel-bound plane
articles.summary: He is being hailed around the world as a hero for helping stop a passenger plane bound for Israel from plunging into the ground, despite his own severe injuries.
articles.body: He is being hailed around the world as a hero for helping stop a passenger plane bound for Israel from plunging into the ground, despite his own severe injuries. Images of Capt. Smit Machchhar covered in blood have gone viral after he fought his fellow pilot, who, according to Israeli officials, stabbed him and attempted to nose-dive the plane carrying 174 people from Dubai to Tel Aviv. While bleeding profusely, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, allowing other passengers and the Emirati crew to overpower the other pilot and take control of the aircraft. The flight was diverted to an airport in Saudi Arabia, where it landed safely. The Mumbai native’s actions have “shown the world the highest form of courage” and “prevented another 9/11 like attack from happening,” Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said Thursday, after speaking with Machchhar’s family. “The whole world is proud of him,” he added. Machchhar spoke previously of getting the “aviation bug” at 19 while pursuing a management course to grow his family’s textile business. He worked for years at a low-cost Indian airline before joining Flydubai, and had nearly 10,000 hours of flying experience before Wednesday’s incident. Machchhar is being treated in a hospital in Tabuk city in northwest Saudi Arabia, with his condition described as “stable” on Wednesday by the Indian Embassy in Riyadh. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told Fox News he was “very badly wounded.” Deepak Mittal, India’s ambassador to the United Arab Emirates, said on X he met with Machhar’s family on Thursday in Dubai and “conveyed full support of the Government of India in ensuring welfare and wellbeing of the Indian Hero.” Netanyahu called Machchhar “a true hero.” “Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door, and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker — preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster,” he said. Machchhar’s former employer, the Indian budget carrier SpiceJet, said on X that he flew for the airline for 10 years. According to his LinkedIn profile, Machchhar joined the Emirati low-cost carrier Flydubai in 2022 after flying for SpiceJet since 2011. On Wednesday, the veteran captain was flying a Boeing 737 Max 8, the newer variant of the 737 plane that Machchhar had nearly 10,000 hours of experience flying, according to his profile and a YouTube podcast interview he gave last year. “My first aircraft was a Boeing, and it’s always been that aircraft all my life,” he said. Machchhar said he had flown challenging routes, dodged bad weather, and handled medical emergencies in the air before. His mother was “scared” when he first told her of his plan to become a pilot, he said in the 2025 interview, but his supportive father agreed to cover the steep fees for aviation training. Between 2008 and 2009, Machchhar trained for 18 months at an aviation college in New Zealand. It was the first time he had been outside India, he said, and he had only been on a “couple of flights” as a passenger before learning to fly. He “stood out” among those training and did well with his studies, Mainland Air chief executive Philip Kean told New Zealand’s 1News, adding: “We’re all very proud of him here.” In his early days as a qualified pilot, he took whatever flight routes he was assigned. “When I started flying ... the only thing I wanted to do then was fly,” Machchhar told the podcast. “I didn’t want to sleep, I didn’t want to go anywhere, and they loved me for it.” “For a pilot to gain that experience and to refine your skills is what a pilot is,” he added. But his attitude changed when he got married and started a family, he said. “Now I would say I try when I get out of the cockpit or the aircraft, I don’t want the other guy to know that I’m a pilot. I don’t want to discuss aviation,” he said. “Now the kids are there,” he said. “They want to play with you.” In the interview, Machchhar also spoke about the “rigorous training” that pilots and cabin crew undergo, which includes safety and emergency procedures. “When we are up there and if something happens, who is going to save you? You’ll be lucky enough to have a doctor on board,” he said. “They can save your life,” he said, referring to the cabin crew.

articles.title: HIV prevention drug hailed as breakthrough, but who gets access?
articles.summary: Lenacapavir, a twice-a-year injection could transform HIV prevention, but it will not be available to all.
articles.body:
A medicine injected just twice a year could transform the fight against HIV.

In a 2024 clinical trial involving more than 2,000 young women in South Africa and Uganda, no participants who received lenacapavir contracted HIV.

Developed by United States pharmaceutical company Gilead Sciences, the injectable drug can be used to prevent HIV.

“It’s the most innovative tool that has reached the HIV arena for the last decade, because it’s the closest we have [to] a vaccine,” Carlota Baptista da Silva, global HIV lead at Doctors Without Borders (known by its French initials, MSF), told Al Jazeera.

The World Health Organization has recommended the long-acting injectable as an additional form of pre-exposure prophylaxis, or PrEP – medicine to reduce the risk of getting HIV.

But the arrival of the drug comes at a challenging juncture in the global fight against HIV.

International funding for HIV fell 18 percent in 2025, to $7.3bn, its lowest level in nearly two decades, according to the United Nations programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS). The squeeze has already hit prevention programmes: The number of people receiving medicine to reduce risk fell from 1.4 million in 2024 to 1.1 million in 2025.

That makes the arrival of a highly effective, twice-yearly prevention option significant. The question of who can access it is now more urgent.

For MSF, the scientific question has largely been answered: lenacapavir can prevent HIV with remarkable efficacy.

The fight now is whether the rules governing manufacture, price and supply will allow that scientific breakthrough to reach the people who need it.

In the United States, lenacapavir costs about $28,000 per person annually. Generic versions are expected to cost about $40 a year.

A generic version is a copy of the original drug made by another manufacturer after the patent holder licenses the technology. It contains the same active ingredient, but it can be produced and sold at a much lower price.

In June 2025, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved lenacapavir for HIV prevention, giving people the option of an injection twice a year. But in several low- and middle-income countries, access to cheaper versions is not expected at scale until 2027.

Gilead is supplying its own version of lenacapavir at no profit for programmes supported by the Global Fund and the US President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), with rollouts under way in countries including South Africa, Kenya, Zambia, Nigeria and Eswatini.

These are not the cheaper generic versions expected to cost about $40 per person a year. Gilead has licensed six manufacturers to produce those, with large-scale generic rollout expected in 2027.

At least 26 middle-income countries are excluded from Gilead’s generics agreement, MSF says, including countries with rising HIV infections and some that helped test the drug. Among them are Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru.

“People should not really help generate the evidence for breakthrough medicine and then find that their country is excluded from affordable generic access,” da Silva said.

According to MSF, countries excluded from the licence accounted for close to 23 percent of new HIV infections globally in 2023.

Gilead has since announced a separate agreement with the Pan American Health Organization, creating an access pathway for 14 Latin American and Caribbean countries outside its generic licensing territory, including Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru.

MSF argues that leaves those countries dependent on Gilead rather than able to automatically buy the cheaper generics.

For more than a year, MSF says it has sought permission to purchase lenacapavir directly from Gilead for its medical programmes, without demanding a discounted price.

“Despite those requests, Gilead has not allowed MSF to purchase this medicine directly,” da Silva said.

That matters particularly in humanitarian emergencies, she argues. People displaced by conflict or disaster may struggle to take a prevention pill every day, while sexual violence and other vulnerabilities can increase the risk of HIV.

Daily PrEP pills are already available as an alternative to the injection. But unlike lenacapavir, they need to be taken consistently to provide protection. An injection offering six months of protection could be particularly valuable.

“People living through conflict [and] humanitarian crises cannot be the last in line for medical innovation,” da Silva said.

Gilead declined Al Jazeera’s request for an interview due to scheduling constraints. In its emailed statement, it said its access strategy combines no-profit supplies, royalty-free licensing and regional agreements. It didn’t reply to questions about why it won’t sell its drug to MSF, or why certain countries were excluded from its generics agreement.

The company plans to provide enough lenacapavir for up to three million people through 2028 as generic manufacturers scale up production, with large-scale generic rollout expected in 2027.

MSF says that is nowhere near the scale required, pointing to projections that close to 20 million people worldwide need access to PrEP to substantially reduce new HIV infections. That includes all forms of PrEP, not just lenacapavir.

But countries left outside Gilead’s generic licensing deal may have another option.

Can governments bypass the patent barriers?

World Trade Organization (WTO) rules allow governments, in some cases, to bypass a drug company’s patent so cheaper versions of a medicine can be made or imported without the company’s permission.

They can also authorise government use of patents and challenge patents they consider weak or unjustified. The 2001 Doha Declaration affirmed WTO members’ right to use such safeguards to protect public health.

Brazil has used them before in the fight against HIV. In 2007, after negotiations with pharmaceutical company Merck over the price of the HIV drug efavirenz failed, Brazil issued a compulsory licence allowing it to access cheaper generic versions of the medicine.

Nearly two decades later, activists are urging Brazil to consider using those powers again for lenacapavir if patent barriers prevent affordable generic access.

MSF says governments excluded from Gilead’s licence could consider those same legal safeguards for lenacapavir, including compulsory licensing, government-use authorisations and challenges to patents.

It is also calling on Gilead to ensure its agreements with generic manufacturers do not prevent them from supplying countries where patent barriers have been removed through such measures.

For MSF, the stakes go beyond lenacapavir. The way the drug is made available could determine whether one of the greatest advances in HIV prevention in decades reaches people based on need, rather than where they live or what their health systems can afford.

“For a humanitarian medical organisation, we should not have to spend more than a year trying to find a way to buy a WHO-recommended medicine,” da Silva said.

articles.title: Tories committed to pension triple lock, deputy leader says
articles.summary: Alex Bughart says pensioners are a 'special case' as there is nothing they can do to increase their income.
articles.body:
Conservative deputy leader Alex Burghart has described pensioners as a "special case" as he reaffirmed the party's commitment to the state pension triple lock.

He argued that retirees deserve different treatment because, once they stop working, they can do "absolutely nothing" to increase their income.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has set out plans to end the existing state pension triple lock from 2030 to help fund a new national care service.

In a round of interviews with BBC local radio stations, Burghart suggested that any "difficult decisions" on welfare should focus on working-age benefits.

He told BBC Radio Berkshire that it was "obvious" there should be two different approaches to welfare – one for pensioners and another for working-age adults.

He said pensioners had "reached the end of their working lives" and there was "nothing they can do to improve their circumstances", adding that they had "a right to be looked after properly".

"The same is not true for people who are working age," he said.

Burghart added: "I just think it's a very practical and decent argument and that most people will understand that."

Asked about adults with disabilities who cannot work, he said his argument applied to "people who can work and should be in work".

The Conservatives have long campaigned for curbs to spending on sickness and disability benefits, including Personal Independence Payments (PIP).

Last year, Sir Keir Starmer faced a major backbench rebellion over proposed cuts to disability benefits, leading to a U-turn which saw the plans substantially watered down.

Speaking on BBC Hereford and Worcester, Burghart suggested Burnham had missed an opportunity to press ahead with the cuts after taking office.

"He didn't do it, and now we're in this very serious problem where this huge budget at the centre of government isn't going to be touched," he said.

The Conservative deputy leader also defended his party's "tough love" approach to unemployment benefits for young people.

He said 18-year-olds leaving school would no longer be able simply to "sign on" the following day.

"You will be able to claim some money but that will require you to turn up to the job centre and under supervision either do a course, or do your job applications or look for work," he said.

Burghart said some young people were signing on "very early in life" and forming "very bad habits" which could be difficult to break.

He argued this "wasn't good for anybody".

Burghart also reaffirmed the Conservatives' "very, very firm" pledge not to enter an electoral pact with Reform UK, either before or after a general election.

He criticised Reform over what he described as "scandal around their money" and referred to donations from people involved in cryptocurrency.

"We do not want to do a deal with those people," he said.

"Kemi [Badenoch] is someone with enormous personal integrity and we are not doing a deal with them."
